bullets.title: Mary Karr, The Art of Memoir No. 1
bullets.note: in the _Paris Review_. This is a simply stunning interview of [Mary Karr](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/nvfohvho3x8x5r/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbi53aWtpcGVkaWEub3JnL3dpa2kvTWFyeV9LYXJy) ([@marykarrlit](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/wwt2hghowk5kv8/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9tYXJ5a2FycmxpdA==)) from 2009. I’ve read it multiple times, highlighted nearly every page, and saved my scans to [Evernote](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/06cwh9h7d9o9wn/aHR0cDovL2V2ZXJub3RlLmNvbQ==). That’s how much goodness I think it contains. It’s also laugh-out-loud funny.

bullets.title: How MDMA is being used to treat PTSD
bullets.note: from** **_The Economist_****.** [This seven-minute video](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/l0aehmhk3n0nve/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj04SzVzSnVUYlF2WQ==) is beautifully done, and I highly recommend a quick watch. Here’s a portion of the description, edited for length: “The FDA has labeled MDMA a breakthrough treatment…. In a recent study, more than 60% of patients no longer met the clinical criteria for PTSD after MDMA treatment. For Jonathan, a suicidal veteran, conventional treatments hadn’t worked. He saw this trial as his last hope, and for him, the treatment was a revelation.”

bullets.title: The Obstacle is the Way
bullets.note:
!** I loved _The_ _Obstacle is the Way_ so much that I actually produced [the audiobook version](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/oehkhqh8r6k6lv/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXVkaWJsZS5jb20vcGQvVGhlLU9ic3RhY2xlLUlzLXRoZS1XYXktQXVkaW9ib29rL0IwMEsyNTJFVDg=). This book has helped me turn problems upside down, manage fear, and even uncover unique opportunities. It’s a collection of stories and principles about Stoicism, which I consider one of the best “operating systems” for thriving in high-stress environments.  
  
The book is worth reading multiple times, and it’s become popular at the highest ranks of the NFL, military, and beyond. Huge thanks to Ryan ([@RyanHoliday](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/wvunxemrraghgpw4zu8/ppueh9h7z2325w/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9SeWFuSG9saWRheS8=)) for signing 100 copies so that I can mail them out as surprise gifts.

bullets.title: “I realized that I could lose myself in a character. I could live in a character. It was a choice. And when I finished with that, I took a month to remember who I was. ‘What do I believe? What are my politics? What do I like and dislike?’ It took me a while, and I was depressed going back into my concerns and my politics. But there was a shift that had already happened. And the shift was, ‘Wait a second. If I can put Jim Carrey aside for four months, who is Jim Carrey? Who the hell is that?’ ... I know now he does not really exist. He’s ideas. ... Jim Carrey was an idea my parents gave me. Irish-Scottish-French was an idea I was given. Canadian was an idea that I was given. I had a hockey team and a religion and all of these things that cobble together into this kind of Frankenstein monster, this representation. It’s like an avatar. These are all the things I am. You are not an actor, or a lawyer. No one is a lawyer. There are lawyers, law is practiced, but no one is a lawyer. There is no one, in fact, there.” — Jim Carrey (@JimCarrey) And, as always, please give me feedback on Twitter. Which bullet above is your favorite? What do you want more or less of? Other suggestions? Let me know! Just send a tweet to @tferriss and put #5BulletFriday at the end so I can find it. Have a wonderful weekend, all! Tim
